title: Projective modules detected by flat local families with injective residue maps
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $M$ be a projective $R$-module, with no finite-generation assumption [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For every prime $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], put $A_{\mathfrak p}=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ and $M_{\mathfrak p}=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}M$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Suppose that $N_{\mathfrak p}$ is a flat $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and that $v_{\mathfrak p}:M\to N_{\mathfrak p}$ is $R$-linear (using restriction of scalars). Let $u_{\mathfrak p}:M_{\mathfrak p}\to N_{\mathfrak p}$ be the induced $A_{\mathfrak p}$-linear map $x/s\mapsto s^{-1}v_{\mathfrak p}(x)$. Assume for every $\mathfrak p$ that its reduction $$M_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak m_{\mathfrak p}M_{\mathfrak p}\longrightarrow N_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak m_{\mathfrak p}N_{\mathfrak p}$$ is injective. Then each $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is projective over $A_{\mathfrak p}$, each $u_{\mathfrak p}$ is universally injective (for every $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module $L$, the map $L\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}\to L\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}N_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]), and the $R$-linear map $$M\longrightarrow\prod_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R}N_{\mathfrak p},\qquad x\longmapsto(v_{\mathfrak p}(x))_{\mathfrak p}$$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, lemma-universally-injective-local, applied prime by prime to the local-to-global product argument in Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, final proof paragraph; general module form of the localized-splitting and annihilator argument.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{\mathfrak p}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-projective] with $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $P=M$. It gives projectivity of $M_{\mathfrak p}$ over $A_{\mathfrak p}$, without a finite-generation assumption.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, lemma-universally-injective-local, hypotheses; projectivity under localization: algebra.tex, Tag 05A3, lemma-ascend-properties-modules (4)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-universal-injective-residue] to the local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and the map $u_{\mathfrak p}$. Step 1 supplies projectivity of the source, and the hypotheses supply flatness of $N_{\mathfrak p}$ and injectivity modulo $\mathfrak m_{\mathfrak p}$. Hence $1_L\otimes u_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective for every $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module $L$, giving the asserted universal injectivity at every prime.

In step 2 take $L=A_{\mathfrak p}$. For any module $T$ over a commutative ring $A$, the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $A\otimes_A T\to T$, $a\otimes t\mapsto at$, inverse to $t\mapsto1\otimes t$: on a generator $a\otimes t$, the other composite is $1\otimes at=a\otimes t$. Under these identifications $1_A\otimes u_{\mathfrak p}$ is $u_{\mathfrak p}$, so every $u_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, specialize universal injectivity to L=A; tensor universal property: algebra.tex, Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product

proof.text: Let $x$ lie in the kernel of the product map. Then $u_{\mathfrak p}(x/1)=v_{\mathfrak p}(x)=0$ for every prime, so step 3 gives $x/1=0$ in every $M_{\mathfrak p}$. If $x\ne0$, the ideal $I=\{r\in R:rx=0\}$ is proper, since $1x=x\ne0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal], choose a prime $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$. The zero criterion of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $sx=0$. But then $s\in I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, a contradiction. Thus the kernel is zero; applying this to a difference proves injectivity.
